context: Dr. Alvarez's Monday lecture surveyed ocean circulation and began by connecting the topic to the previous unit. context: The organization adopted this equipment lending policy to make routine decisions consistent across departments. It applies to staff and registered students, provided all required records are current. The standard limit is 14 days. Requests beyond that limit are not automatically denied, but they must be reviewed by the designated administrator before any commitment is made. The ordinary requirement is one 7-day renewal; verbal permission does not substitute for the recorded approval. Missing a required return, response, or reporting deadline triggers a consequence of $15 per day. Staff should document the event in the central system so that later reviewers can distinguish an approved exception from an oversight. The policy does not apply in the usual way to medical equipment. context: The Orchid API service is intended for internal applications that need predictable automated access. Clients connect using HTTPS on port 443. Every request must include the credential in the X-Orchid-Key header; credentials in query strings are rejected because URLs may be logged. The default service limit is 120 requests per minute per project. Bursts above the limit receive error 429, and clients should retry with exponential backoff rather than immediately repeat the request. Successful create operations return an identifier that can be checked at /v2/jobs/{id}. Status responses distinguish queued, running, completed, and failed work. Clients should treat unknown fields as forward-compatible additions and must not depend on field ordering. Completed operational records are retained for 24 hours, after which the service may remove them without another notice. Deleting a client-side reference does not cancel server-side work. Cancellation is accepted only while a job is queued or running, and a completed job cannot be reopened. Timestamps use UTC in ISO 8601 form. Text is UTF-8, numeric sizes are bytes, and an omitted optional value differs from an explicit zero. Client logs should retain request identifiers so support can trace failures without receiving credential values. The service team publishes maintenance windows at least two business days ahead when possible. Sandbox credentials cannot access production records.
